title: Molecular classification of human papillomavirus-positive cervical cancers based on immune signature enrichment.
authors: Song, Guanghui; Luo, Jiangti; Zou, Shaohan; Lou, Fang; Zhang, Tianfang; Zhu, Xiaojun; Yang, Jianhua; Wang, Xiaosheng
one_liner_zh: 该文基于免疫特征富集对HPV阳性宫颈癌进行分子分型，属于纯转录组表达与临床关联分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模，亦无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus-positive (HPV+) cervical cancers are highly heterogeneous in clinical and molecular characteristics. Thus, an investigation into their heterogeneous immunological profiles is meaningful in providing both biological and clinical insights into this disease. METHODS: Based on the enrichment of 29 immune signatures, we discovered immune subtypes of HPV+ cervical cancers by hierarchical clustering. To explore whether this subtyping method is reproducible, we analyzed three bulk and one single cell transcriptomic datasets. We also compared clinical and molecular characteristics between the immune subtypes. RESULTS: Clustering analysis identified two immune subtypes of HPV+ cervical cancers: Immunity-H and Immunity-L, consistent in the four datasets. In comparisons with Immunity-L, Immunity-H displayed stronger immunity, more stromal contents, lower tumor purity, proliferation potential, intratumor heterogeneity and stemness, higher tumor mutation burden, more neoantigens, lower levels of copy number alterations, lower DNA repair activity, as well as better overall survival prognosis. Certain genes, such as MUC17, PCLO, and GOLGB1, showed significantly higher mutation rates in Immunity-L than in Immunity-H. 16 proteins were significantly upregulated in Immunity-H vs. Immunity-L, including Caspase-7, PREX1, Lck, C-Raf, PI3K-p85, Syk, 14-3-3_epsilon, STAT5-alpha, GATA3, Src_pY416, NDRG1_pT346, Notch1, PDK1_pS241, Bim, NF-kB-p65_pS536, and p53. Pathway analysis identified numerous immune-related pathways more highly enriched in Immunity-H vs. Immunity-L, including cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity, antigen processing and presentation, T/B cell receptor signaling, chemokine signaling, supporting the stronger antitumor immunity in Immunity-H vs. Immunity-L. CONCLUSION: HPV+ cervical cancers are divided into two subgroups based on their immune signatures' enrichment. Both subgroups have markedly different tumor immunity, progression phenotypes, genomic features, and clinical outcomes. Our data offer novel perception in the tumor biology as well as clinical implications for HPV+ cervical cancer.
abstract_zh: 背景：人乳头瘤病毒阳性（HPV+）宫颈癌在临床和分子特征上具有高度异质性。因此，研究其异质性免疫谱系对于提供该疾病的生物学和临床见解具有重要意义。方法：基于29个免疫特征的富集情况，我们通过层次聚类发现了HPV+宫颈癌的免疫亚型。为探讨该分型方法的可重复性，我们分析了三个批量转录组数据集和一个单细胞转录组数据集。我们还比较了不同免疫亚型之间的临床和分子特征。结果：聚类分析确定了HPV+宫颈癌的两种免疫亚型：Immunity-H和Immunity-L，在四个数据集中结果一致。与Immunity-L相比，Immunity-H表现出更强的免疫力、更多的基质成分、更低的肿瘤纯度、增殖潜力、瘤内异质性和干性，更高的肿瘤突变负荷、更多的新抗原，更低的拷贝数变异水平、更低的DNA修复活性，以及更好的总生存预后。某些基因，如MUC17、PCLO和GOLGB1，在Immunity-L中的突变率显著高于Immunity-H。与Immunity-L相比，Immunity-H中有16种蛋白质显著上调，包括Caspase-7、PREX1、Lck、C-Raf、PI3K-p85、Syk、14-3-3_epsilon、STAT5-alpha、GATA3、Src_pY416、NDRG1_pT346、Notch1、PDK1_pS241、Bim、NF-kB-p65_pS536和p53。通路分析识别出许多在Immunity-H中比Immunity-L更富集的免疫相关通路，包括细胞因子-细胞因子受体相互作用、自然杀伤细胞介导的细胞毒性、抗原加工和呈递、T/B细胞受体信号传导、趋化因子信号传导，支持Immunity-H比Immunity-L具有更强的抗肿瘤免疫力。结论：基于免疫特征的富集情况，HPV+宫颈癌被分为两个亚组。这两个亚组在肿瘤免疫、进展表型、基因组特征和临床结局方面存在显著差异。我们的数据为HPV+宫颈癌的肿瘤生物学和临床意义提供了新的见解。
